functions.name: ZMusic_GetLastError
functions.description: Returns a human-readable description of the most recent error reported by the ZMusic library. Intended for diagnostics after a prior call failed.
requirements: Call after an operation that may fail to retrieve a meaningful message.
The returned pointer is owned by the library and must not be freed by the caller.
Thread-safety and lifetime of the returned string beyond subsequent library calls are unknown.

functions.name: ZMusic_SetCallbacks
functions.description: Installs application-provided callbacks for message reporting and optional soundfont virtualization/IO. Use to integrate logging and custom soundfont management.
requirements: callbacks may be NULL to disable callbacks; otherwise it must point to a valid ZMusicCallbacks struct that remains valid for as long as the library may use it.
MessageFunc is optional; without it, messages go to stdout.
If any of the soundfont management callbacks (OpenSoundFont, SF_OpenFile, SF_AddToSearchPath, SF_Close) are set, all must be set.
PathForSoundfont is only needed if the client virtualizes soundfont names; otherwise may be NULL.
NicePath is optional; if not provided, paths must not contain client-specific tokens.

functions.name: ZMusic_SetGenMidi
functions.description: Supplies GenMIDI instrument data needed for OPL playback. Without this, the OPL synth will not function.
requirements: data must point to valid GenMIDI data; exact format/size unspecified in this header.
The ownership/lifetime requirements for data are unknown; assume it must remain valid until the library has consumed or copied it.

functions.name: ZMusic_SetWgOpn
functions.signature: void ZMusic_SetWgOpn(const void* data, unsigned len);
functions.description: Sets the default OPN (Yamaha FM) bank. Without this, OPN only works with custom banks.
requirements: data must point to a buffer of length len containing the OPN bank data.
len must match the size of the provided bank data.
Lifetime/ownership of data beyond the call is unknown.

functions.name: ZMusic_SetDmxGus
functions.signature: void ZMusic_SetDmxGus(const void* data, unsigned len);
functions.description: Supplies DMXGUS configuration/data to enable the GUS synth to run in actual GUS mode.
requirements: data must point to a buffer of DMXGUS data of length len.
len must be the exact size of the DMXGUS data.
Lifetime/ownership of data beyond the call is unknown.

functions.name: ZMusic_GetConfiguration
functions.description: Returns a read-only array of all available configuration options. The array is terminated by an empty entry with all fields set to 0/NULL.
requirements: Treat the returned array as read-only and do not free it.
Iterate until an entry where all elements are 0/NULL to detect termination.

functions.name: ZMusic_IdentifyMIDIType
functions.description: Identifies the MIDI file type of a data buffer for use by MIDI dumpers and related tools.
requirements: id must point to a buffer containing the data to identify; size is the buffer length in bytes.
id must be non-NULL and size must be >= 0.
The function reads but does not modify the buffer.

functions.name: ZMusic_CreateMIDISource
functions.signature: ZMusic_MidiSource ZMusic_CreateMIDISource(const uint8_t* data, size_t length, EMIDIType miditype);
functions.description: Creates an opaque MIDI source object from a memory buffer and declared MIDI type. Used as input for operations like rendering/dumping.
requirements: data must point to a buffer of at least length bytes containing the MIDI content.

requirements: source must be a valid ZMusic_MidiSource created by ZMusic_CreateMIDISource.

samplerate must be a positive integer.
devtype selects the backend; devarg may be backend-specific and may be NULL if not required.

functions.name: ZMusic_FillStream

requirements: stream must be a valid ZMusic_MusicStream.
buff must be a non-NULL pointer to writable memory of at least len bytes.

functions.name: ZMusic_Start

functions.name: ZMusic_Pause
functions.description: Pauses playback of the given music stream.

functions.name: ZMusic_Resume

functions.name: ZMusic_Update

functions.name: ZMusic_IsPlaying

requirements: song must be a valid ZMusic_MusicStream.

functions.name: ZMusic_Stop
functions.description: Stops playback of the given music stream.

functions.name: ZMusic_Close
functions.description: Closes and releases the given music stream and any associated resources.

requirements: song must be a valid ZMusic_MusicStream.
info must be a non-NULL pointer to writable SoundStreamInfoEx.

generators.generator:
import random
from typing import List

# Generator for GenMIDI-like data. The exact format is unspecified in the header,
# but historically GenMIDI lumps used by OPL synths (e.g., in Doom) contain:
# - a signature (e.g., b'GENMIDI' or MIDI-like),
# - instrument count and tables,
# - per-instrument operator parameter blocks (~36-60 bytes each).
# Since the API only requires a non-empty pointer and the fuzzer stub only checks for
# non-empty input, we focus on producing plausible, self-consistent binary blobs that
# resemble known structures to exercise different parsing paths while remaining valid-like.

MAX_SIZE = 4096

SIGS = [
    b"GENMIDI\x00",           # classic id
    b"#OPLGENMIDI\x00",       # alt tagged header
    b"ADLMIDI\x00",           # some tools use different tags
    b"GMID\x00\x00\x00\x00", # short tag padded
]


def _rand_bytes(r: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes(r.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(n))


def _make_pseudo_genmidi_table(r: random.Random, instruments: int) -> bytes:
    # Construct a pseudo instrument table. Each instrument gets a small header and
    # two operator blocks (OPL is 2-operator typically). Keep sizes bounded.
    # We'll create per-instrument fixed-size 48-byte records to look structured.
    recs: List[bytes] = []
    for i in range(instruments):
        # Program number (0-127), bank, flags
        prog = i % 128
        bank = r.randrange(0, 8)
        flags = r.randrange(0, 4)
        hdr = bytes([prog, bank, flags, 0])
        # Operator blocks: 2 x 22 bytes of plausible OPL params
        def opblk():
            # ADSR, KSL, mult, feedback, wave, levels, etc.
            vals = [
                r.randrange(0, 128),  # attack/decay
                r.randrange(0, 128),  # sustain/release
                r.randrange(0, 4) | (r.randrange(0, 4) << 4),  # KSL/mult packed-ish
                r.randrange(0, 8),    # feedback
                r.randrange(0, 8),    # waveform
                r.randrange(0, 64),   # total level
                r.randrange(0, 2),    # keyscale
                r.randrange(0, 2),    # vib
                r.randrange(0, 2),    # trem
                r.randrange(0, 2),    # sustain enable
            ]
            # pad to 22 bytes with random but bounded values
            while len(vals) < 22:
                vals.append(r.randrange(0, 256))
            return bytes(vals[:22])
        op1 = opblk()
        op2 = opblk()
        # Padding to reach 48 bytes total per record
        pad_len = 48 - (len(hdr) + len(op1) + len(op2))
        if pad_len < 0:
            # Shouldn't happen, but guard
            pad_len = 0
        pad = _rand_bytes(r, pad_len)
        recs.append(hdr + op1 + op2 + pad)
    return b"".join(recs)


def _make_block_with_directory(r: random.Random, instruments: int) -> bytes:
    # Some GenMIDI-like formats start with a directory of offsets to instrument records
    # followed by the instrument data. We lay out a small header + count + offsets.
    header = r.choice(SIGS)
    count = instruments
    # directory of 4-byte little-endian offsets
    records = []
    dir_entries = []
    # Start after header + count(4) + dir(count*4)
    dir_size = 4 * count
    base = len(header) + 4 + dir_size
    cur = base
    for _ in range(count):
        rec = _make_pseudo_genmidi_table(r, 1)  # one record block
        records.append(rec)
        dir_entries.append(cur)
        cur += len(rec)
    # Build directory
    dir_bytes = b"".join(int(x).to_bytes(4, 'little') for x in dir_entries)
    count_bytes = int(count).to_bytes(4, 'little')
    blob = header + count_bytes + dir_bytes + b"".join(records)
    return blob


def _make_minimal_header_block(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # For very small inputs, still look like a header + a couple of instruments
    header = r.choice(SIGS)
    n = r.randrange(1, 8)
    table = _make_pseudo_genmidi_table(r, n)
    return header + int(n).to_bytes(4, 'little') + table


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)
    # Choose a construction strategy
    strategy = r.randrange(0, 3)
    if strategy == 0:
        instruments = r.randrange(1, 64)
        blob = _make_block_with_directory(r, instruments)
    elif strategy == 1:
        instruments = r.randrange(16, 128)
        header = r.choice(SIGS)
        table = _make_pseudo_genmidi_table(r, instruments)
        blob = header + int(instruments).to_bytes(4, 'little') + table
    else:
        blob = _make_minimal_header_block(r)

    # Ensure size bounds and non-empty
    if len(blob) > MAX_SIZE:
        blob = blob[:MAX_SIZE]
    if not blob:
        blob = b"GENMIDI\x00\x01\x00\x00\x00"  # fallback minimal non-empty
    return blob

import random
from typing import List

# Generator for OPN bank data (Yamaha OPN FM bank), opaque to the API.
# Goal: produce valid-looking, self-consistent binary with internal structure
# resembling known OPN patch/bank layouts so the callee can parse/accept it.
# We avoid malformed fuzzing; instead we craft plausible banks of varying sizes.

MAGIC_OPNB = b"OPNB"  # synthetic magic to help parsers that tolerate tags
MAGIC_TFI  = b"TFI0"  # common simple FM instrument header marker (fictional tag kept opaque)
MAGIC_END  = b"END!"

# Common numbers to exercise different code paths (small, typical, large)
INSTR_COUNTS = [1, 16, 32, 64, 128]

# Operator parameter ranges for OPN (YM2612-like). Values kept in valid ranges.
# These are chosen to be plausible and to cover edge/extreme combinations.
RANGE = {
    "algo": (0, 7),              # algorithm 0..7
    "fb": (0, 7),                # feedback 0..7
    # Per-operator parameters
    "mul": (0, 15),              # frequency multiple
    "dt": (0, 7),                # detune
    "tl": (0, 127),              # total level
    "ar": (0, 31),               # attack rate
    "dr": (0, 31),               # decay rate
    "sr": (0, 31),               # sustain rate
    "rr": (0, 15),               # release rate
    "sl": (0, 15),               # sustain level
    "ssg": (0, 15),              # SSG-EG
}

def _rand_u(rng: random.Random, lo: int, hi: int) -> int:
    return rng.randint(lo, hi)

def _pack_u8(val: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes((val & 0xFF,))

def _pack_u16le(val: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes((val & 0xFF, (val >> 8) & 0xFF))

def _make_op_params(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Order chosen to be consistent and simple: mul, dt, tl, ar, dr, sr, rr, sl, ssg
    fields = [
        _rand_u(rng, *RANGE["mul"]),
        _rand_u(rng, *RANGE["dt"]),
        _rand_u(rng, *RANGE["tl"]),
        _rand_u(rng, *RANGE["ar"]),
        _rand_u(rng, *RANGE["dr"]),
        _rand_u(rng, *RANGE["sr"]),
        _rand_u(rng, *RANGE["rr"]),
        _rand_u(rng, *RANGE["sl"]),
        _rand_u(rng, *RANGE["ssg"]),
    ]
    return bytes(fields)

def _make_instrument(rng: random.Random, include_name: bool) -> bytes:
    out = bytearray()
    # Header marker per instrument
    out += MAGIC_TFI
    # Global instrument params
    algo = _rand_u(rng, *RANGE["algo"])  # 0..7
    fb   = _rand_u(rng, *RANGE["fb"])    # 0..7
    out += _pack_u8(algo)
    out += _pack_u8(fb)
    # 4 operators worth of parameters
    for _ in range(4):
        out += _make_op_params(rng)
    # Optional name (0-terminated), 0..12 chars typical
    if include_name:
        namelen = rng.randint(0, 12)
        # Choose readable ASCII to aid any logging/paths
        name = bytes(rng.choice(b"ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789-_ ") for _ in range(namelen))
        out += name + b"\x00"
    return bytes(out)

def _make_bank(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    out = bytearray()

    # Bank header: magic + version + flags
    out += MAGIC_OPNB
    version = rng.choice([0x0001, 0x0002])
    out += _pack_u16le(version)

    # Flags bitfield: bit0=has names, bit1=has checksum, bit2=reserved
    has_names = rng.choice([True, False])
    has_checksum = rng.choice([True, False])
    flags = (1 if has_names else 0) | ((2 if has_checksum else 0))
    out += _pack_u8(flags)

    # Instrument count and reserved
    count = rng.choice(INSTR_COUNTS)
    out += _pack_u16le(count)
    out += _pack_u16le(0)  # reserved

    # Optional bank-level metadata blob
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        meta = bytearray()
        # simple TLV-like: type(1) len(1..32) val
        entries = rng.randint(0, 3)
        for _ in range(entries):
            t = rng.randint(1, 4)
            l = rng.randint(1, 32)
            v = bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(l))
            meta += _pack_u8(t) + _pack_u8(l) + v
        out += _pack_u16le(len(meta))
        out += meta
    else:
        out += _pack_u16le(0)

    # Instruments
    for i in range(count):
        out += _make_instrument(rng, include_name=has_names)

    # Optional padding to align
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        pad_to = rng.choice([4, 8, 16])
        pad = (-len(out)) % pad_to
        if pad:
            out += bytes(pad)

    # Trailer with an index table for quick lookup (offsets to each instrument)
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        # Build simple offset table: write tag, count, then count 32-bit LE offsets
        out += b"IDXT"
        # To generate offsets, we must rescan. Easiest: append table after building instruments by remembering sizes.
        # For simplicity, we will approximate: regenerate with same RNG stream would differ, so instead compute by scanning markers.
        # Instruments are prefixed by MAGIC_TFI; scan to collect their starts.
        data = bytes(out)
        starts: List[int] = []
        idx = data.find(MAGIC_TFI, 0)
        while idx != -1 and len(starts) < count:
            starts.append(idx)
            idx = data.find(MAGIC_TFI, idx + 1)
        # Pack table
        out += _pack_u16le(len(starts))
        for off in starts:
            out += _pack_u16le(off & 0xFFFF)  # short offsets to keep table compact
    # Optional checksum
    if has_checksum:
        out += b"CKS1"
        checksum = sum(out) & 0xFFFF
        out += _pack_u16le(checksum)

    # End marker
    out += MAGIC_END

    # Cap to 4096 bytes per requirements; if larger, drop optional parts by truncation
    return bytes(out[:4096])


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    """Generate a deterministic, valid-looking OPN bank byte buffer.
    The buffer is sized <= 4096 bytes and varies with the input seed.
    """
    return _make_bank(seed)

import random
from typing import List

def _gus_patch_name(note: int) -> bytes:
    # 14-char name, uppercase letters/numbers/underscore. Common GUS patch naming style.
    charset = b"ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789_"
    name = bytearray()
    for _ in range(14):
        name.append(random.choice(charset))
    return bytes(name)

def _le16(v: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes((v & 0xFF, (v >> 8) & 0xFF))

def _le32(v: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes((v & 0xFF, (v >> 8) & 0xFF, (v >> 16) & 0xFF, (v >> 24) & 0xFF))

def _make_gus_patch(sample_rate: int, bits16: bool, loop: bool) -> bytes:
    # Create a plausible GUS .PAT-like header + trivial sample data.
    # Magic "GF1PATCH110" then NUL padding to 60 bytes title field in classic spec.
    title = b"GF1PATCH110\x00" + b"MinimalPatch\x00"
    title = title[:60] + b"\x00" * max(0, 60 - len(title))

    instruments = 1
    header = title
    header += _le16(instruments)  # instrument count
    header += _le16(0)            # voices
    header += _le32(0)            # channels

    # Instrument header
    inst_name = _gus_patch_name(60)
    inst_size = 0  # not accurate, but many readers ignore
    inst_hdr = inst_name + _le32(inst_size) + _le16(1)  # one layer

    # Layer header
    layer_size = 0
    samples = 1
    layer_hdr = _le32(layer_size) + _le16(samples) + b"\x00" * 40

    # Sample header (simplified). Real .PAT is more complex; craft consistent values.
    # Use 32-byte sample name.
    sname = (_gus_patch_name(0) + b"\x00" * 32)[:32]
    data_len = 512 if bits16 else 1024  # bytes of PCM data
    loop_start = 64
    loop_end = 256 if loop else 64
    mode = 1 if loop else 0
    smp_flags = (2 if bits16 else 1)  # pretend flags: 1=8bit,2=16bit
    base_note = 60  # middle C
    finetune = 0

    samp_hdr = (
        sname +
        _le32(data_len) +
        _le32(loop_start) +
        _le32(loop_end) +
        _le16(mode) +
        _le16(smp_flags) +
        _le32(sample_rate) +
        _le32(base_note) +
        _le32(finetune) +
        b"\x00" * 24  # pad
    )

    # PCM data: generate a simple triangle/saw to be non-silent.
    if bits16:
        # 16-bit little endian PCM
        period = 32
        vals: List[int] = []
        for i in range(data_len // 2):
            t = i % period
            v = int(((t / (period - 1)) * 2 - 1) * 12000)
            vals.append(v)
        pcm = b"".join(_le16((v + 65536) % 65536) for v in vals)
    else:
        # 8-bit unsigned PCM
        period = 64
        vals2: List[int] = []
        for i in range(data_len):
            t = i % period
            v = int(((t / (period - 1)) * 2 - 1) * 60) + 128
            vals2.append(max(0, min(255, v)))
        pcm = bytes(vals2)

    blob = header + inst_hdr + layer_hdr + samp_hdr + pcm
    return blob

def _make_dmxgus_cfg(entries: int, include_header: bool) -> bytes:
    # Create a simple DMXGUS-like cfg mapping program numbers to patch names.
    # Typical lines like: 0 piano.pat
    lines = []
    if include_header:
        lines.append(b"; DMXGUS configuration\r\n")
        lines.append(b"[Patch Names]\r\n")
    used = set()
    for prog in range(entries):
        name = _gus_patch_name(prog).lower().replace(b" ", b"_")
        # Ensure extension
        if not name.endswith(b".PAT".lower()):
            name = name + b".pat"
        if name in used:
            # tweak to make unique
            name = name[:-4] + b"_%d.pat" % prog
        used.add(name)
        lines.append(str(prog).encode('ascii') + b" " + name + b"\r\n")
    return b"".join(lines)

def _pack_multi(files: List[bytes]) -> bytes:
    # Create a very simple concatenated package: [count][len][data]...
    # Little-endian 32-bit lengths. This is opaque to library but can be used by custom loaders.
    out = bytearray()
    out += _le32(len(files))
    for f in files:
        out += _le32(len(f))
        out += f
    return bytes(out)

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    random.seed(seed)

    # Choose one of several valid shapes of DMXGUS-related data:
    #  - a plausible DMXGUS.cfg text
    #  - a single GUS patch (.PAT-like) binary
    #  - a small package containing a cfg and several patches
    choice = random.choice(["cfg", "pat", "pkg"])  # keep simple

    if choice == "cfg":
        entries = random.randint(16, 128)
        include_header = random.choice([True, False])
        data = _make_dmxgus_cfg(entries, include_header)
        return data[:4096]

    if choice == "pat":
        sr = random.choice([11025, 16000, 22050, 32000, 44100])
        bits16 = random.choice([True, False])
        loop = random.choice([True, False])
        data = _make_gus_patch(sr, bits16, loop)
        return data[:4096]

    # pkg
    entries = random.randint(8, 32)
    cfg = _make_dmxgus_cfg(entries, True)
    patches = []
    for _ in range(min(entries, 6)):
        sr = random.choice([11025, 22050, 44100])
        bits16 = random.choice([True, False])
        loop = random.choice([True, False])
        patches.append(_make_gus_patch(sr, bits16, loop))
    pkg = _pack_multi([cfg] + patches)
    return pkg[:4096]

import random
import struct
from typing import List, Tuple

# This generator produces valid MIDI-family buffers that exercise ZMusic_IdentifyMIDIType
# and ZMusic_CreateMIDISource. We synthesize several small but valid formats:
# - Standard MIDI File (SMF) type 0/1 with minimal tracks and meta events
# - MUS (Doom MUS) with header and minimal event stream
# - HMI/XMI simple headers with minimal payload
# - MIDS minimal recognizable header
# The buffers are constructed to be valid and within 4096 bytes.

# Utility: variable-length quantity for MIDI

def _vlq(n: int) -> bytes:
    n = max(0, int(n))
    out = bytearray()
    out.append(n & 0x7F)
    n >>= 7
    while n:
        out.insert(0, 0x80 | (n & 0x7F))
        n >>= 7
    return bytes(out)

# Build a minimal SMF file
# type_: 0 or 1; tracks: 1 or 2; ppqn: typical 480

def _build_smf(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)
    fmt = r.choice([0, 1])
    ntrks = 1 if fmt == 0 else r.choice([1, 2])
    ppqn = r.choice([96, 120, 192, 240, 480])
    header = b"MThd" + struct.pack(
        ">IHHH", 6, fmt, ntrks, ppqn
    )

    def make_track() -> bytes:
        trk = bytearray()
        # Delta 0: tempo meta (120 BPM = 500000 us/qn)
        trk += _vlq(0)
        trk += b"\xFF\x51\x03" + struct.pack(
            ">I", 500000
        )[1:]  # 3 bytes
        # Delta small: program change ch0
        trk += _vlq(r.randint(0, 10))
        trk += bytes([0xC0 | 0, r.randint(0, 127)])
        # Note on
        note = r.choice([60, 62, 64, 67, 69])
        vel = r.randint(64, 100)
        trk += _vlq(r.randint(0, 10))
        trk += bytes([0x90 | 0, note, vel])
        # Hold for some ticks
        trk += _vlq(r.randint(30, 120))
        # Note off
        trk += bytes([0x80 | 0, note, 64])
        # End of track
        trk += _vlq(0) + b"\xFF\x2F\x00"
        return b"MTrk" + struct.pack(">I", len(trk)) + bytes(trk)

    tracks = b"".join(make_track() for _ in range(ntrks))
    return header + tracks

# Build a minimal Doom MUS file
# Based on MUS format: header "MUS\x1A", score length/offset, channels, etc.
# We'll place a very short event stream ending with 0x60 end marker.

def _build_mus(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed ^ 0xC0FFEE)
    id_ = b"MUS\x1A"
    score_len = 0  # fill later
    score_ofs = 0  # fill later
    channels = 4
    sec_channels = 0
    instrcnt = 0
    dummy = 0
    header = bytearray()
    header += id_
    header += struct.pack("<HHHHHH", score_len, score_ofs, channels, sec_channels, instrcnt, dummy)
    # No instrument list as instrcnt=0

    # Build simple events per MUS encoding
    events = bytearray()
    # MUS event: Note on on channel 0, note 60, volume present
    # Event byte: 0 (channel) | 0x00 event type (release note=0, play note=1, etc.) -> play note is 0x10
    # MUS format specifics: We'll use play note (0x10), with volume bit (0x80) set to include volume byte.
    # For robustness we use: event = chan | 0x10 | 0x80
    chan = 0
    events.append((chan & 0x0F) | 0x10 | 0x80)
    events.append(60)  # note
    events.append(80)  # volume
    # Add a small time delta (variable length; set continuation bit on previous event) -> time tag 1
    # In MUS, time tag follows an event with 0x40 flag; instead, we emit another event with 0x40 to indicate time advance.
    events.append((chan & 0x0F) | 0x00 | 0x40)  # release note with time flag just to advance time
    # Termination event: 0x60 indicates score end
    events.append(0x60)

    score_ofs = len(header)
    score_len = len(events)
    # Patch header values
    header[4:4+2] = struct.pack("<H", score_len)
    header[6:6+2] = struct.pack("<H", score_ofs)

    return bytes(header) + bytes(events)

# Build a minimal HMI file
# HMI is Human Machine Interfaces format (Miles). We provide recognizable header and minimal chunk.

def _build_hmi(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed ^ 0xBEEF)
    # Many HMI files start with "HMI-MIDISONG" or "HMI-MIDISONG061595"
    hdr = b"HMI-MIDISONG" + (b"061595" if r.choice([True, False]) else b"")
    # Followed by some header fields. We'll append minimal plausible bytes.
    # We'll include a fake chunk table and trivial data to keep parser happy.
    body = bytearray()
    body += struct.pack("<I", 0)  # version or flags placeholder
    body += struct.pack("<I", 1)  # number of tracks
    # Track offset after this table
    track_offset = len(hdr) + 8 + 8  # rough
    body += struct.pack("<I", track_offset)
    body += struct.pack("<I", 0)  # reserved
    # Minimal track: small data with an end marker 0xFC for EOT in some parsers
    track = bytearray()
    track += b"\x00\xC0\x00"  # delta 0, program change 0
    track += b"\x00\x90\x3C\x50"  # delta 0, note on
    track += b"\x10\x80\x3C\x40"  # delta 16, note off
    track += b"\x00\xFF\x2F\x00"  # End of track in MIDI-like streams
    return hdr + bytes(body) + bytes(track)

# Build a minimal XMI file (Extended MIDI used by Miles/AdLib)

def _build_xmi(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed ^ 0x1234)
    # XMI RIFF-like IFF: FORM XDIR or FORM XMID; we craft FORM XMID with CAT info
    # IFF chunk: 4-byte id, 4-byte big-endian size, payload
    def iff_chunk(id4: bytes, payload: bytes) -> bytes:
        return id4 + struct.pack(">I", len(payload)) + payload

    # TIMB and EVNT are common chunks
    timb = b""  # empty instrument map
    # Minimal EVNT: tick rate and some events; here simple Miller format: delta, event bytes, 0xFF 0x2F 0x00
    ev = bytearray()
    ev += b"\x00\xC0\x00"  # program change
    ev += b"\x00\x90\x3C\x50"  # note on
    ev += b"\x14\x80\x3C\x40"  # wait and note off
    ev += b"\x00\xFF\x2F\x00"  # end
    form_payload = iff_chunk(b"TIMB", timb) + iff_chunk(b"EVNT", bytes(ev))
    form = b"FORM" + struct.pack(">I", len(b"XMID") + len(form_payload)) + b"XMID" + form_payload
    return form

# Build a minimal MIDS (Windows game MIDS) recognizable header with small event stream

def _build_mids(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed ^ 0xDEAD)
    # Some MIDS begin with "MIDS" and a little-endian size. We'll craft that with a tiny payload.
    payload = bytearray()
    payload += b"\x00\x00\x00\x00"  # flags/timebase placeholder
    # Embed a small MIDI-like stream
    payload += b"\x00\xC0\x00\x00\x90\x3C\x50\x14\x80\x3C\x40\x00\xFF\x2F\x00"
    return b"MIDS" + struct.pack("<I", len(payload)) + bytes(payload)

# Dispatcher to choose a format to generate

def _pick_format(r: random.Random) -> Tuple[str, bytes]:
    choice = r.choice(["smf", "mus", "hmi", "xmi", "mids", "smf"])  # bias toward SMF
    if choice == "smf":
        return choice, _build_smf(r.getrandbits(32))
    if choice == "mus":
        return choice, _build_mus(r.getrandbits(32))
    if choice == "hmi":
        return choice, _build_hmi(r.getrandbits(32))
    if choice == "xmi":
        return choice, _build_xmi(r.getrandbits(32))
    if choice == "mids":
        return choice, _build_mids(r.getrandbits(32))
    return "smf", _build_smf(r.getrandbits(32))

# Public API

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)
    fmt, data = _pick_format(r)
    # Ensure size limits and non-empty
    if not data:
        data = _build_smf(seed ^ 0x55AA)
    # Trim conservatively if ever exceeding limit
    if len(data) > 4096:
        data = data[:4096]
    return bytes(data)

def _rand_filename(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Assemble a name with varied components.
    parts: List[str] = []

    # Optionally add a relative prefix path
    if r.random() < 0.7:
        parts.append(r.choice(REL_PREFIXES).rstrip("/"))

    # Optionally include a directory or two with diverse characters
    num_dirs = r.randint(0, 2)
    for _ in range(num_dirs):
        dirlen = r.randint(3, 12)
        base = ''.join(r.choice(SAFE_CHARS + EXTRA_CHARS) for _ in range(dirlen)).strip()
        # sanitize Windows-forbidden chars if present
        base = ''.join(c for c in base if c not in FORBIDDEN_CHARS_WIN)
        if not base:
            base = "d"
        # Avoid trailing dots/spaces on Windows by trimming
        base = base.rstrip(' .') or "dir"
        parts.append(base)

    # Core filename
    name_len = r.randint(3, 16)
    base = ''.join(r.choice(SAFE_CHARS + EXTRA_CHARS) for _ in range(name_len)).strip()
    base = ''.join(c for c in base if c not in FORBIDDEN_CHARS_WIN)
    if r.random() < 0.25:
        base += r.choice(UNICODE_PARTS)
    base = base.strip('. ')
    if not base:
        base = "file"

    # Choose extension based on intended use: input MIDI for OpenSongFile or output WAV/SMF
    # Since the same generator feeds all stubs, mix extensions.
    ext_choice = r.random()
    if ext_choice < 0.45:
        ext = r.choice(MIDI_EXTS)
    elif ext_choice < 0.75:
        ext = r.choice(AUDIO_EXTS)
    else:
        ext = r.choice(OTHER_EXTS)

    filename = base + ext

    # Avoid reserved device names as final element on Windows
    if filename.upper().split('.')[0] in SPECIAL_NAMES:
        filename = "file_" + filename

    parts.append(filename)

    # Join parts into a relative path
    # Normalize to use forward slashes which most runtimes accept; fuzzing harness may map accordingly
    path = "/".join(p for p in parts if p)

    # Ensure length bounds and no empty
    if not path:
        path = "file.mid"
    if len(path) > 300:  # keep path reasonable
        path = path[-300:]

    return path


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)

    # Occasionally return a bare temp-like name to encourage writable simple paths
    mode = r.random()
    if mode < 0.2:
        name = f"fuzz_{r.randint(0, 1_000_000)}" + r.choice(MIDI_EXTS + AUDIO_EXTS + OTHER_EXTS)
    else:
        name = _rand_filename(r)

    # Ensure it is a relative writable path (avoid root or drive letters)
    if os.path.isabs(name):
        name = os.path.basename(name)

    # Make sure parent directories are expressed but not created (harness handles temp env)
    # Avoid trailing slash
    name = name.rstrip("/")
    if not name:
        name = "file.mid"

    # Enforce max overall size and NUL-terminate
    b = name.encode('utf-8')[:4095]
    return b + b"\x00"

import random
import struct
import zlib

# This generator focuses on producing valid music file bytes that ZMusic_OpenSongMem
# can recognize and open. We generate a variety of well-formed small MIDI-like files:
# - Standard MIDI File (SMF) type 0 and type 1 with minimal events
# - MUS (Doom MUS) header with a small valid payload
# - HMI/XMI minimal placeholders are less standardized; we stick to SMF and MUS for validity
# The function returns bytes suitable for FUZZ_PARAM_STR() in the fuzzer stub.
# Size is kept small (<4KB) and content is deterministic with the seed but varied.

META_TEMPO_EVENT = b"\xff\x51\x03"  # Set Tempo, 3-byte payload
TIME_SIG_EVENT = b"\xff\x58\x04"     # Time Signature, 4-byte payload
KEY_SIG_EVENT = b"\xff\x59\x02"      # Key Signature, 2-byte payload
END_OF_TRACK = b"\x00\xff\x2f\x00"   # delta=0, End of Track


def _vlq(n: int) -> bytes:
    # Variable Length Quantity encoder for MIDI
    if n == 0:
        return b"\x00"
    out = []
    out.append(n & 0x7F)
    n >>= 7
    while n:
        out.append(0x80 | (n & 0x7F))
        n >>= 7
    out.reverse()
    return bytes(out)


def _midi_header(fmt: int, tracks: int, division: int = 480) -> bytes:
    return b"MThd" + struct.pack(
        ">IHHH", 6, fmt, tracks, division
    )


def _midi_track(events: bytes) -> bytes:
    return b"MTrk" + struct.pack(
        ">I", len(events)
    ) + events


def _note_on(chan: int, note: int, vel: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes([0x90 | (chan & 0x0F), note & 0x7F, vel & 0x7F])


def _note_off(chan: int, note: int, vel: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes([0x80 | (chan & 0x0F), note & 0x7F, vel & 0x7F])


def _program_change(chan: int, prog: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes([0xC0 | (chan & 0x0F), prog & 0x7F])


def _control_change(chan: int, ctrl: int, val: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes([0xB0 | (chan & 0x0F), ctrl & 0x7F, val & 0x7F])


def _meta_event(delta: int, meta: bytes, payload: bytes) -> bytes:
    return _vlq(delta) + meta + bytes([len(payload)]) + payload


def _build_smf_type0(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    ppqn = rng.choice([96, 120, 240, 480])
    tempo_usq = rng.choice([500000, 750000, 333333])  # 120, 80, 180 BPM
    time_sig = (rng.choice([2,3,4,5,7]), rng.choice([2,3,4]))
    key_sf = rng.randint(-7, 7)
    key_minor = rng.randint(0, 1)

    events = bytearray()
    # Meta: tempo, time signature, key signature
    events += _meta_event(0, META_TEMPO_EVENT, struct.pack(
        ">I", tempo_usq)[1:]  # 3 bytes
    )
    events += _meta_event(0, TIME_SIG_EVENT, bytes([
        time_sig[0] & 0xFF, time_sig[1] & 0xFF, 24, 8
    ]))
    events += _meta_event(0, KEY_SIG_EVENT, bytes([(key_sf + 256) % 256, key_minor]))

    # Channel setup
    chan = rng.randrange(0, 9)  # avoid channel 9 (10th) percussion sometimes
    prog = rng.randrange(0, 128)
    events += b"\x00" + _program_change(chan, prog)
    # Optional CCs
    if rng.random() < 0.6:
        events += _vlq(rng.choice([0, 10])) + _control_change(chan, 7, rng.randrange(64, 127))  # volume
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        events += _vlq(0) + _control_change(chan, 10, rng.randrange(0, 127))  # pan

    # A few notes forming a chord or arpeggio
    base = rng.choice([48, 52, 55, 57, 60, 62, 64, 67])
    pattern = rng.choice([
        [0, 4, 7],
        [0, 3, 7],
        [0, 5, 7, 12],
        [0, 2, 4, 7],
    ])
    dur_ticks = rng.choice([ppqn//4, ppqn//2, ppqn])

    # Start notes at delta 0 as a chord
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        for i, step in enumerate(pattern):
            delta = 0 if i == 0 else 0
            events += _vlq(delta) + _note_on(chan, base + step, rng.randrange(80, 120))
        # hold and release together
        events += _vlq(dur_ticks) + _note_off(chan, base + pattern[0], 64)
        for step in pattern[1:]:
            events += _vlq(0) + _note_off(chan, base + step, 64)
    else:
        # Arpeggiate with small gaps
        gap = max(1, dur_ticks // max(2, len(pattern) * 2))
        for i, step in enumerate(pattern):
            delta = gap if i else 0
            events += _vlq(delta) + _note_on(chan, base + step, rng.randrange(80, 120))
            events += _vlq(gap) + _note_off(chan, base + step, 64)

    # End track
    events += END_OF_TRACK

    return _midi_header(0, 1, ppqn) + _midi_track(bytes(events))


def _build_smf_type1(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    ppqn = rng.choice([96, 192, 480])
    tempo_usq = rng.choice([400000, 500000, 600000])

    # Track 0: tempo map and markers
    t0 = bytearray()
    t0 += _meta_event(0, META_TEMPO_EVENT, struct.pack(
        ">I", tempo_usq)[1:])
    t0 += _meta_event(0, TIME_SIG_EVENT, bytes([4, 2, 24, 8]))
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        # Add a track name
        name = b"ZMusic Fuzz SMF"
        t0 += _vlq(0) + b"\xff\x03" + bytes([len(name)]) + name
    t0 += END_OF_TRACK

    # Track 1: simple melody
    t1 = bytearray()
    chan = rng.randrange(0, 9)
    t1 += _vlq(0) + _program_change(chan, rng.randrange(0, 128))
    base = rng.choice([60, 62, 64, 65, 67])
    for i in range(rng.randrange(4, 9)):
        pitch = base + rng.choice([0, 2, 4, 5, 7, 9, 12])
        dur = rng.choice([ppqn//4, ppqn//3, ppqn//2])
        gap = rng.choice([0, ppqn//8])
        vel = rng.randrange(70, 120)
        t1 += _vlq(gap) + _note_on(chan, pitch, vel)
        t1 += _vlq(dur) + _note_off(chan, pitch, 64)
    t1 += END_OF_TRACK

    return _midi_header(1, 2, ppqn) + _midi_track(bytes(t0)) + _midi_track(bytes(t1))


def _build_mus(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Minimal valid MUS file (Doom MUS). We create a header and a few simple events.
    # MUS header structure:
    # 0: id "MUS\x1A"
    # 4: score len (uint16)
    # 6: score start (uint16)
    # 8: channels (uint16)
    # 10: sec channels (uint16)
    # 12: instr count (uint16)
    # 14: dummy/unused (uint16)
    # 16: instrument data (instr count * uint16)
    # Followed by score data starting at score start
    
    # We'll include 0 instruments and a tiny score with a couple of notes and an end marker.
    channels = 8
    instr_count = 0
    score_start = 16  # immediately after header when no instrument table

    # Build score events (variable length). We use simple note-on/off and end.
    # MUS event encoding:
    # First byte: [event_type(4 bits) | channel(4 bits)]
    # Followed by event-specific bytes, with last event in time slice marked by 0x80 in the first byte.
    # We'll put all in single time slice and then a time marker and end (0x6) event.

    # Helpers
    EVT_RELEASE = 0  # Key off
    EVT_PRESS = 1    # Key on
    EVT_PITCH = 2    # Pitch wheel (not used)
    EVT_SYS = 6      # System event, 0 is end of score

    def ev(byte0, *rest, last=False):
        b0 = (byte0 | (0x80 if last else 0x00)) & 0xFF
        return bytes([b0, *rest])

    chan = rng.randrange(0, min(15, channels-1))
    note = rng.randrange(50, 72)
    vel = rng.randrange(64, 127)

    score = bytearray()
    # Note on
    score += ev((EVT_PRESS << 4) | chan, note & 0x7F, vel & 0x7F, last=True)
    # Time delta: variable length; we use 0x00 (no time advance) then another slice with duration
    # MUS time marker uses values with high bit set for continuation; we just use small single byte delta
    score += b"\x00"  # advance 0 ticks (optional)
    # Note off in next slice
    score += ev((EVT_RELEASE << 4) | chan, note & 0x7F, last=True)
    # End of score system event in its own slice
    score += ev((EVT_SYS << 4) | 0, 0, last=True)

    score_len = len(score)

    header = bytearray()
    header += b"MUS\x1A"
    header += struct.pack("<HHHHH", score_len, score_start, channels, 0, instr_count)
    header += struct.pack("<H", 0)  # padding/dummy

    mus = bytes(header) + bytes(score)
    return mus


def _wrap_as_riff_wave(rng: random.Random, midi_bytes: bytes) -> bytes:
    # Some backends may accept RIFF RMID (MIDI inside RIFF). Build a minimal RIFF with MThd chunk.
    # RIFF('RMID') { LIST('INFO')..., data('MThd'.. + 'MTrk'..)} is common, but simplest is RIFF('RMID') with a 'data' chunk containing MIDI.
    data_chunk = b"data" + struct.pack("<I", len(midi_bytes)) + midi_bytes
    riff_size = 4 + len(data_chunk)
    riff = b"RIFF" + struct.pack("<I", riff_size) + b"RMID" + data_chunk
    return riff


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    choice = rng.random()

    # Weighted choices: prefer SMF for broad compatibility, then SMF-in-RIFF, then MUS
    if choice < 0.5:
        data = _build_smf_type0(rng)
    elif choice < 0.8:
        data = _build_smf_type1(rng)
    elif choice < 0.9:
        # Wrap a small SMF as RIFF RMID
        midi = _build_smf_type0(rng)
        data = _wrap_as_riff_wave(rng, midi)
    else:
        data = _build_mus(rng)

    # Optionally compress with DEFLATE and prepend a tiny magic used by some containers? Not necessary.
    # Keep under 4096 bytes
    if len(data) > 4096:
        data = data[:4096]
    return data

# This generator creates valid small audio sample files as byte buffers.
# It focuses on WAV (RIFF) with PCM/float data and optional LIST/INFO and cue/adtl
# plus smpl chunk holding loop points. It also can emit minimal AIFF and Ogg Vorbis
# headers with small payloads, to exercise format sniffers and loop tag scanners.
# Size is kept under 4096 bytes.

_MAX_SIZE = 4096

def _chunk_id(s: str) -> bytes:
    return s.encode('ascii')

def _pad2(b: bytes) -> bytes:
    return b + (b"\x00" if (len(b) & 1) else b"")

def _wav_fmt_chunk(bits: int, channels: int, rate: int, sample_format: str) -> bytes:
    # sample_format: 'pcm' or 'float'
    if sample_format == 'pcm':
        audio_format = 1  # PCM
        block_align = channels * (bits // 8)
        byte_rate = rate * block_align
        fmt_body = struct.pack('<HHIIHH', audio_format, channels, rate, byte_rate, block_align, bits)
    else:
        audio_format = 3  # IEEE float
        block_align = channels * 4
        byte_rate = rate * block_align
        bits = 32
        fmt_body = struct.pack('<HHIIHH', audio_format, channels, rate, byte_rate, block_align, bits)
    return _chunk_id('fmt ') + struct.pack('<I', len(fmt_body)) + fmt_body

def _wav_data_chunk(channels: int, bits: int, frames: int, waveform: str) -> bytes:
    # Generate simple waveform samples
    samples: List[int] = []
    if bits == 8:
        # unsigned 8-bit PCM
        for n in range(frames):
            v = int(127 + 100 * (1 if (waveform == 'square' and (n // 8) % 2 == 0) else 0))
            if waveform == 'saw':
                v = (n % 64) * 4
            elif waveform == 'silence':
                v = 128
            v = max(0, min(255, v))
            for _ in range(channels):
                samples.append(v)
        payload = bytes(samples)
    elif bits == 16:
        for n in range(frames):
            if waveform == 'square':
                v = 16000 if (n // 16) % 2 == 0 else -16000
            elif waveform == 'saw':
                v = (n % 128) * 256 - 16384
            elif waveform == 'silence':
                v = 0
            else:
                v = int(20000 if (n % 32) < 16 else -20000)
            v = max(-32768, min(32767, v))
            for _ in range(channels):
                samples.append(v & 0xFFFF)
        payload = struct.pack('<' + 'h' * (len(samples)), *[(s if s < 32768 else s - 65536) for s in samples])
    else:  # float32
        fsamp: List[float] = []
        for n in range(frames):
            if waveform == 'square':
                v = 0.7 if (n // 32) % 2 == 0 else -0.7
            elif waveform == 'saw':
                v = ((n % 256) / 255.0) * 2 - 1
            elif waveform == 'silence':
                v = 0.0
            else:
                v = 0.5 if (n % 64) < 32 else -0.5
            for _ in range(channels):
                fsamp.append(float(v))
        payload = struct.pack('<' + 'f' * len(fsamp), *fsamp)
    chunk = _chunk_id('data') + struct.pack('<I', len(payload)) + payload
    return _pad2(chunk)

def _wav_list_info(tags: List[Tuple[str, str]]) -> bytes:
    # LIST/INFO with simple Ixxx tags
    info_payload = b''
    for fourcc, value in tags:
        valb = value.encode('utf-8') + b'\x00'
        info_payload += _chunk_id(fourcc) + struct.pack('<I', len(valb)) + _pad2(valb)
    list_body = _chunk_id('INFO') + info_payload
    return _chunk_id('LIST') + struct.pack('<I', len(list_body)) + _pad2(list_body)

def _wav_cue_and_adtl(frames: int, rate: int, loops: List[Tuple[int, int]]) -> bytes:
    # Create cue points and associated adtl/ltxt text labels
    cue_entries = []
    adtl = b''
    cue_id = 1
    for start, end in loops:
        # clamp
        s = max(0, min(frames - 1, start))
        e = max(s + 1, min(frames, end))
        # cue for start
        cue_entries.append(struct.pack('<I4sIIIII', cue_id, b'data', 0, 0, 0, s, 0))
        label = f'loop_start_{cue_id}'.encode('ascii') + b'\x00'
        adtl += _chunk_id('labl') + struct.pack('<I', 4 + len(label)) + struct.pack('<I', cue_id) + _pad2(label)
        cue_id += 1
        # cue for end
        cue_entries.append(struct.pack('<I4sIIIII', cue_id, b'data', 0, 0, 0, e, 0))
        label = f'loop_end_{cue_id}'.encode('ascii') + b'\x00'
        adtl += _chunk_id('labl') + struct.pack('<I', 4 + len(label)) + struct.pack('<I', cue_id) + _pad2(label)
        cue_id += 1
    cue_chunk = b''
    if cue_entries:
        body = struct.pack('<I', len(cue_entries)) + b''.join(cue_entries)
        cue_chunk = _chunk_id('cue ') + struct.pack('<I', len(body)) + _pad2(body)
    adtl_chunk = b''
    if adtl:
        adtl_body = _chunk_id('adtl') + adtl
        adtl_chunk = _chunk_id('LIST') + struct.pack('<I', len(adtl_body)) + _pad2(adtl_body)
    return cue_chunk + adtl_chunk

def _wav_smpl(loops: List[Tuple[int, int]], rate: int) -> bytes:
    # smpl chunk with loop definitions
    if not loops:
        return b''
    # Fixed header (manufacturer, product, samplePeriod, MIDI unity note, pitch fraction, SMPTE, etc.)
    sample_period_ns = int(1e9 / max(1, rate))
    header = struct.pack('<IIIIIIII', 0, 0, sample_period_ns, 60, 0, 0, 0, len(loops))
    loop_entries = b''
    loop_id = 0
    for start, end in loops:
        if end <= start:
            end = start + 1
        loop_entries += struct.pack('<IIIIII', loop_id, 0, start, end, 0, 0)
        loop_id += 1
    body = header + loop_entries
    return _chunk_id('smpl') + struct.pack('<I', len(body)) + _pad2(body)

def _build_wav(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Choose parameters
    channels = rng.choice([1, 2])
    sample_format = rng.choice(['pcm', 'float'])
    if sample_format == 'pcm':
        bits = rng.choice([8, 16])
    else:
        bits = 32
    rate = rng.choice([11025, 22050, 32000, 44100])
    frames = rng.randint(64, 1024)
    waveform = rng.choice(['square', 'saw', 'silence'])

    # Optional chunks
    add_info = rng.random() < 0.6
    add_cue = rng.random() < 0.5
    add_smpl = rng.random() < 0.7

    loops: List[Tuple[int, int]] = []
    if add_cue or add_smpl:
        # create 1-2 loop regions
        for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 2)):
            s = rng.randint(0, max(0, frames - 8))
            e = rng.randint(s + 1, min(frames, s + rng.randint(8, max(9, frames // 2))))
            loops.append((s, e))

    fmt = _wav_fmt_chunk(bits, channels, rate, sample_format)
    data = _wav_data_chunk(channels, bits, frames, waveform)

    chunks = [fmt]
    if add_info:
        tags = []
        if rng.random() < 0.7:
            tags.append(('INAM', rng.choice(['Test Tone', 'Looped Sample', 'Silence'])))
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            tags.append(('IART', rng.choice(['ZMusic', 'Fuzzer'])))
        chunks.append(_wav_list_info(tags))
    if add_cue:
        chunks.append(_wav_cue_and_adtl(frames, rate, loops))
    if add_smpl:
        chunks.append(_wav_smpl(loops, rate))
    chunks.append(data)

    riff_body = _chunk_id('WAVE') + b''.join(chunks)
    riff = _chunk_id('RIFF') + struct.pack('<I', len(riff_body)) + riff_body
    return riff[:_MAX_SIZE]

def _build_aiff(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Minimal AIFF with PCM16 mono/stereo
    channels = rng.choice([1, 2])
    frames = rng.randint(64, 1024)
    bits = 16
    rate = rng.choice([22050, 44100])

    # AIFF uses 80-bit float for sample rate; use common pre-encoded 44100/22050 constants
    def _ieee_extended(rate_val: int) -> bytes:
        # Encode simplistic 80-bit extended for common rates
        if rate_val == 44100:
            return bytes.fromhex('400E AC44 0000 0000 0000')  # approximate
        if rate_val == 22050:
            return bytes.fromhex('400D AC44 0000 0000 0000')
        return bytes.fromhex('400E AC44 0000 0000 0000')

    # COMM chunk
    comm_body = struct.pack('>hIh', channels, frames, bits) + _ieee_extended(rate)
    comm = _chunk_id('COMM') + struct.pack('>I', len(comm_body)) + comm_body

    # SSND chunk with small silent payload
    block_offset = 0
    block_size = 0
    # simple data
    data_samples = [0] * (frames * channels)
    data_payload = struct.pack('>' + 'h' * len(data_samples), *data_samples)
    ssnd_body = struct.pack('>II', block_offset, block_size) + data_payload
    ssnd = _chunk_id('SSND') + struct.pack('>I', len(ssnd_body)) + ssnd_body

    form_body = _chunk_id('AIFF') + comm + ssnd
    form = _chunk_id('FORM') + struct.pack('>I', len(form_body)) + form_body
    return form[:_MAX_SIZE]

def _build_ogg_vorbis(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Construct minimal Ogg container with Vorbis identification header page only.
    # Many decoders will reject as incomplete, but format identification and tag scanners may read headers.
    # Ogg page header fields
    def ogg_page(header_type, granule_pos, serial, seq, segment_table: bytes, seg_payload: bytes) -> bytes:
        header = b'OggS'  # capture pattern
        version = b'\x00'
        header_type_flag = bytes([header_type])
        gp = struct.pack('<Q', granule_pos)
        s = struct.pack('<I', serial)
        sn = struct.pack('<I', seq)
        chksum = b'\x00\x00\x00\x00'  # leave zero; some readers ignore
        seg_count = bytes([len(segment_table)])
        page = header + version + header_type_flag + gp + s + sn + chksum + seg_count + segment_table + seg_payload
        return page

    # Vorbis identification packet
    rate = rng.choice([22050, 44100])
    channels = rng.choice([1, 2])
    id_hdr = b'\x01' + b'vorbis' + struct.pack('<I', 0)  # version 0
    id_hdr += bytes([channels])
    id_hdr += struct.pack('<I', rate)
    id_hdr += struct.pack('<I', 0)  # bitrate max
    id_hdr += struct.pack('<I', 64000)  # nominal
    id_hdr += struct.pack('<I', 0)  # min
    id_hdr += bytes([0xB8])  # blocksize 0/1
    id_hdr += b'\x01'  # framing flag

    # Segment table: single segment length
    segs = bytes([len(id_hdr)])
    page0 = ogg_page(header_type=0x02, granule_pos=0, serial=0x12345678, seq=0, segment_table=segs, seg_payload=id_hdr)
    return page0[:_MAX_SIZE]

def _maybe_mix_formats(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Randomly choose a container to build, bias towards WAV for broad decoder support
    choice = rng.choices(['wav', 'aiff', 'ogg'], weights=[0.7, 0.15, 0.15], k=1)[0]
    if choice == 'wav':
        return _build_wav(rng)
    elif choice == 'aiff':
        return _build_aiff(rng)
    else:
        return _build_ogg_vorbis(rng)

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    data = _maybe_mix_formats(rng)
    # Ensure non-empty and within size
    if not data:
        return _build_wav(rng)
    if len(data) > _MAX_SIZE:
        data = data[:_MAX_SIZE]
    return bytes(data)
